attributes.morphology: alternating layers of recrystallized and worked material

evidence.quote:
A typical microstructure of an as-extruded 
 Mo-2Re-Hf-C alloy is shown in figure 1. 
The general appearance of the extruded alloys consisted of alternating layers of recrys - 
tallized and worked material. Twenty to 90 percent of the total area was recrystallized 
following this hot-working operation.

At 1650' C about 5 per - 
cent of the structure was recrystallized, and after annealing at 1930' C, the alloy was 
completely recrystallized.

Creep testing at 1650' C generally 
resulted in complete recrystallization of the matrix and growth of the uniformly dis - 
persed, fine particles into a sparse and erratic dispersion of large (40 to 1200 nm) 
particles.

In figures 4 and 5, transmission electron micrographs of two of the swaged, HfC-precipitate -strengthened Mo-2Re alloys display a uniform dispersion of fine particles 
as small as 5 nm in diameter and a network of pinned dislocations.

After tensile testing 
at 1315' C an increase in dislocation density was observed. Although the fine -particle 
dispersion appeared to be unchanged, there was a decided increase in the number of 
large platelet particles.

It has been assumed in this report that a stoichiometric HfC phase precipitates from 
the Mo or Mo-2Re matrix as fine, uniformly dispersed particles and that these second - 
phase particles are primarily responsible for the strength increases observed.

A typical microstructure of an as-extruded 
 Mo-2Re-Hf-C alloy is shown in figure 1.

tallized and worked material. Twenty to 90 percent of the total area was recrystallized 
following this hot-working operation.
